thumbnailAlt: Original accepted synthetic acoustic receiver histories.
title: Check the wave before connecting the exhaust.
summary: A restricted acoustic benchmark now transports a small pressure pulse with much less numerical distortion. A one-way cylinder-state interface works too, with its external energy source clearly declared.
revision: ENGINE SIMULATOR / ACOUSTIC ACCURACY AND INTERFACES
evidence: Accepted linear-acoustic benchmarks · real exhaust validation pending
heroAlt: Restricted benchmark accuracy improvement distinguished from general exhaust prediction.
heroCaption: Accuracy is attached to a domain: stationary uniform medium, constant wave speed and area, small disturbances and exact grid/time alignment.

sections.title: The first passing solver still had an important limitation
sections.text: The first linear-acoustic module passed its declared travel, reflection and discrete energy tests. Its first-order transport nevertheless smeared the pulse materially: the finest reflected waveform error was about 40.45% of the initial signal RMS, and about 42.69% of the pulse energy was lost numerically. Those are numerical errors, not physical wall damping. Closing an energy budget alone did not make the waveform accurate.

sections.title: Improve a narrow benchmark before widening its claims
sections.text: The next accepted method moves each characteristic by exactly one cell per timestep in this uniform, stationary, constant-wave-speed benchmark. It brings transport and reflection errors near roundoff under those aligned conditions. Receiver sampling still limits peak-time resolution. The graph shows the original rigid-termination histories; it is not a nonlinear hot-exhaust or tuned-pipe calculation.

figure.alt: Two original receiver pressure-perturbation histories show the incident pulse and rigid-end return.
figure.caption: 561 saved samples per receiver, normalized time τ = c t / L. The 1 m pipe, 50 Pa initial pulse and reference gas are synthetic qualification inputs, not chosen Wahoo exhaust dimensions or operating conditions.

sections.title: Separate energy that leaves from energy lost numerically
sections.text: With a rigid end the aligned benchmark retains its discrete pulse energy; with an absorbing end that energy exits through the boundary. Independent pressure/velocity boundary sums check the ledger, and tiny nonzero summation residuals remain in the evidence. This result does not establish physical damping, arbitrary timestep accuracy, variable-area transport, mean-flow effects or nonlinear blowdown.

figure.alt: Stored acoustic energy remains in the rigid case and leaves through the absorbing termination.
figure.caption: All 561 samples per curve retained. Stored acoustic energy is measured in joules; it must not be relabelled as transported gas enthalpy or engine work.

sections.title: Connect a provider without hiding who supplies the energy
sections.text: A separate accepted adapter uses a held-volume gas provider, a newly prescribed small heat cycle and an independently advancing phase clock to gate an acoustic boundary. Its returning-wave checks allow the boundary to absorb as well as supply energy. The acoustic work comes from an explicitly external driver; it is not deducted from the closed-mass cylinder provider.

figure.alt: One-way provider-to-acoustic boundary shows the separate external-driver energy ledger.
figure.caption: The held volume and independent phase clock are synthetic interface conditions. No mass exchange or globally conservative physical cylinder/exhaust engine is represented.

sections.title: Do not turn an acoustic pressure into an upstream gas state
sections.text: Acoustic pressure perturbation, absolute reference pressure, velocity and acoustic energy have different meanings from reservoir total state, mass flux and enthalpy. The newer pressure-driven gas modules retain their own contracts. A real junction needs a separately verified agreement on mass, species, total energy, momentum and time. Matching plots or convenient connectors cannot supply that missing physics.

sections.title: Use the visuals to inspect evidence, not to create it
sections.text: Saved curves and mechanism views help explain these modules. They must retain their independent clocks and model labels rather than appear to be one synchronized firing engine. The latest saved-results prototype passed data/package checks, while its original browser UI gate remained incomplete. No new CAD surfaces, physical exhaust tuning, torque, power or safe operating speed were established by that prototype.
